title: C-melody sax, 'Christine' and playing the Pensacola ballpark pavilion
summary: Hall played a C-melody and copied the record 'Christine'; the band played an open-air pavilion with advertising before dances and battles with rival bands.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: was he playing alto or tenor or a band?

no he had I come to think about it I believe he between Edmund Hall and Edmund Washington they had a C melody sax in there some kind of way I believe that first song that Edmund Hall had was a C melody that's what it was but he had a fast year he could hear a tune and then once and then play it down because he couldn't he could spell it but he couldn't read but after he would learn the melody then Edmund Washington would take and play the second part you see a lot of times Edmund Hall they would switch because he was so fast he could pick up a number so much you know what I mean he could grasp a number even grasp the harmony part see now the band clicked we played at the place called this was a dance hall in the baseball part you see and it was an opening air pavilion and we did the same thing the bands in Pensacola were doing the same thing like we were doing there they used to advertise before the dance that night and we used to have battle royals in there like when Prince or Morris would have Lee Collins they were still there Kathy was still there when they'd advertise the same thing we'd meet on the corn we'd book just like we did here and I stayed there let's see that was 19 24 April I said we left New Orleans and we stayed in Pensacola I won't mention the years but anyhow we got to branching out like we started going to places like like Mobile and I can tell you the first time we went to Mobile we didn't do so good but after the people hurt us we had a number because we had a number Evan Hall was playing the old a white band called the Our band had put it out and I think the number was Christine the number on there was Christine Evan Hall had copied that number off that record and had a minor part to it you know and he used to really play that horn on that number which horn? that was a sax it wasn't his clan then because he used to double on both of them you see I have that record
